about.title: Trinidad Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Trinidad is a small place. With around 367 residents living above the harbor, a death here is rarely a headline and almost never a stranger. It is a neighbor, a fishing partner, someone whose truck you recognized on Patricks Point Drive. When that loss traces back to another person's carelessness, California gives certain family members a way to hold the responsible party accountable through a civil wrongful death claim. Public records for 2025 list one injury collision in Trinidad and no traffic deaths, which reflects how quiet the town's roads usually are. Still, fatal harm can come from many directions: a collision on US-101 or Scenic Drive, a fall on unsafe property, a medical error, a defective product. The claim itself does not depend on a criminal charge and proceeds separately from any prosecution. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Humboldt County families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death matters on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Trinidad Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then extending to certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're connected with can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Help meeting the two-year deadline
items.desc: Most California wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. An early conversation protects your right to bring the claim at all.

items.title: A full picture of what can be recovered
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative died after a crash on US-101 near Trinidad, but no one was charged. Can we still bring a claim?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal case, and it does not require charges or a conviction. The question in civil court is whether someone's negligence caused the death, which is a different and generally lower standard than criminal guilt. An attorney can review the CHP or Humboldt County collision report and evaluate the facts on their own terms.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there are none, the claim can pass to certain other heirs, and some financially dependent family members may also qualify. Because these rules can get complicated in blended or extended families, it helps to have an attorney confirm who should be named before a case is filed.

items.question: How long do we have to act, and does it matter who was responsible?
items.answer: In general, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity is involved, such as a claim tied to a public road or a public agency, a formal claim must usually be presented much sooner, often within six months. Given that shorter window, families in Trinidad are wise to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting for grief to settle.
